sections.title: 1. Agreement, issuing company and priority
sections.body: AGGELOS Rentals is the trading name. The lessor is the legal entity identified on the rental agreement, with its registered address, VAT number and contact details. These terms cover the vehicle type, location and period expressly agreed. The signed rental particulars and individually agreed special conditions prevail over conflicting general wording, subject to mandatory law. A PDF export, stored signature or reprint does not retrospectively amend an earlier agreement or prove acceptance of revised terms. This version applies when supplied and accepted for the relevant rental.

sections.title: 2. Rental period, price and taxes
sections.body: Daily rentals use 24-hour periods. Monthly rentals run between the exact agreed start and end dates; a calendar month is not automatically 30 days. Pickup and return times are those recorded on the agreement, without a universal noon default. The agreed total, any insurance charge, advance payment, balance and billing basis must be stated separately. A quoted price is not proof of payment; an unconfirmed payment is not treated as zero. Agreed extensions and credits are included in the recorded total without duplicate charging. Customer prices and fees below include applicable VAT unless a signed special condition expressly gives the final tax-inclusive amount. Applicable taxes must be disclosed before confirmation.

sections.title: 3. Included services and additional charges
sections.body: Third-party liability insurance is included. CDW, theft protection and other waivers apply only if selected and recorded; they are not automatically included in every rental. Included mileage and assistance are defined below and in the agreement. Airport, port, villa or other delivery/collection, one-way return, out-of-hours service, ferry permissions and optional extras are chargeable only where applicable, disclosed and agreed. An agreed total cannot be increased unilaterally after confirmation. An unpriced service or unspecified penalty is not an automatic charge.

sections.title: 4. Driver eligibility and documentation
sections.body: Each authorised driver must present an original valid driving licence for the actual vehicle category and a passport or national photo ID. An International Driving Permit or official translation is required only where Greek law requires it for the licence concerned, together with the original licence; non-EU nationality alone is not sufficient reason to demand an IDP. The published car policy is minimum age 24, or 26 for premium/luxury cars, and maximum age 74 without surcharge. The applicable minimum licence-holding period of one or two years and any age surcharge must be confirmed before booking. Scooter, motorcycle, ATV and buggy eligibility must be checked for that category; a car licence is not presumed sufficient. Hire may be refused for an invalid/disqualified licence, missing previously disclosed documents or a documented safety/insurance restriction. Refusal and any retained payment must follow the disclosed booking conditions and applicable law.

sections.title: 5. Payments, advances and security deposits
sections.body: Rental payment and any security deposit are separate. The issuing office confirms accepted payment methods before booking; card, bank transfer or IRIS arrangements apply where expressly accepted. Any required card type, named cardholder, security amount, preauthorisation, release process and expected bank-processing delay must be disclosed and recorded. No universal security amount, credit-card-only rule or zero-deposit promise is implied. A deposit is not automatically the insurance excess or a rental payment. Third-party payments require appropriate authorisation. Additional debits require a valid authorisation and an itemised contractual basis; disputed liability is not established merely by taking payment.

sections.title: 6. Mileage - Antiparos, Paros and Piraeus
sections.body: Antiparos and Paros car rentals have unlimited mileage unless a different vehicle-specific condition is agreed. For Piraeus short-term car rentals the published allowance is 150 km per 24 hours unless a different allowance is recorded. Monthly Piraeus rentals use the expressly agreed cumulative allowance and measurement period, not an automatic 150 km multiplied by the rental days. A 2,000 km monthly or whole-rental limit applies only where written; its starting odometer and any extension/proration must be clear. The final VAT-inclusive excess-kilometre rate must be recorded. Where the agreement states EUR 0.20/km, EUR 0.20 is the final charge and VAT is not added again. No conflicting general tariff replaces an individually agreed rate.

sections.title: 7. Insurance, CDW, theft and excess
sections.body: Compulsory third-party liability applies according to the actual policy and Greek law, including the applicable statutory minimum cover; obsolete approximate maximum figures do not limit that cover. CDW/TW, reduced-excess RDW and zero-excess SCDW apply only if available for the vehicle, expressly purchased and shown on the agreement. The actual excess and any security deposit must be stated. EUR 1,500 excess applies only to rentals recording that amount; it is not a universal rule. Zero excess does not by itself mean all risks or equipment are covered. The renter must receive the applicable cover, exclusions and claims procedure before acceptance. Ordinary negligence is not automatically treated as intentional damage or an unlimited waiver of purchased protection.

sections.title: 8. Insurance exclusions and responsibility
sections.body: Tyres, wheels, glass, mirrors, roof, underside, interior, mechanical parts, locks/keys, wrong fuel, towing and personal belongings may be excluded only as set out in the applicable disclosed policy/waiver. Deliberate damage, intoxication, unauthorised driving or prohibited use may affect cover where the policy and law permit; there is no blanket statement that every traffic offence cancels all insurance. The renter is responsible for attributable loss within the agreed protection and applicable law. Additional sums beyond an excess require a distinct disclosed basis, evidence and explanation; the same loss cannot be recovered twice. Statutory third-party protection and the insurer's legal obligations are not waived by these terms.

sections.title: 9. Vehicle category, authorised use and borders
sections.body: A booking is for the confirmed vehicle group unless a make/model is expressly guaranteed. A suitable equivalent or upgrade may be offered without an unagreed surcharge; a material change requires agreement. Only listed authorised drivers may drive. Driving must comply with Greek law. Racing, towing, overloading, unsuitable cargo, driving under alcohol/drugs, use outside suitable paved roads, and use incompatible with the vehicle are prohibited. Border crossing is not permitted. Ferry travel requires prior written permission identifying the islands and route. No restriction removes rights or duties that mandatory law preserves.

sections.title: 10. Handover, condition and maintenance
sections.body: Pickup and return locations are those agreed, including any expressly arranged customer delivery. Record the odometer, fuel, visible damage and relevant mechanical issues jointly where possible. Photographs and documents are retained with the rental and may be supplied as a separate numbered appendix; an empty damage-marker list is not certification of no damage. Return the vehicle in its recorded condition, allowing normal fair wear. The renter must use reasonable care, monitor warnings, tyres and fluids, stop safely when a fault appears and notify the office. Repairs require prior approval except urgent safety action reasonably necessary. Pre-existing faults and ordinary mechanical breakdown are not automatically charged to the renter.

sections.title: 11. Accidents, theft and assistance
sections.body: Notify the issuing office immediately when safe after an accident, theft, loss or breakdown, and contact the Police/emergency services where required, especially injury, theft or a third-party incident. Provide a truthful report, photographs and available official documents promptly, normally within 24 hours where reasonably possible. Preserve evidence and cooperate with the insurer; unavoidable delay does not automatically remove statutory rights. Assistance included for an ordinary covered breakdown is distinct from an optional assistance package (published price EUR 5/day) or attributable recovery costs. Coverage area, exclusions and any extra service must be disclosed. Replacement depends on safety, availability, location and insurance; no unconditional 24-hour replacement promise is made.

sections.title: 12. Damage assessment and loss of use
sections.body: Damage claims must identify the new damage, compare handover/return evidence and provide an itemised estimate or invoice from a competent repairer. The renter may request supporting evidence and dispute a claim. Towing, transfer, administration and loss-of-use claims require the disclosed contractual basis, actual attributable loss and a reasonable documented amount; they are not automatically imposed regardless of fault. Loss of use cannot be assumed for an arbitrary period or duplicated with another recovery. The renter is not liable for loss attributable solely to a pre-existing fault, ordinary breakdown or the lessor's own responsibility.

sections.title: 13. Fuel, smoking, cleaning and animals
sections.body: Return fuel at the recorded pickup level. Missing fuel is charged for the quantity reasonably required at the transparently disclosed rate, plus the published EUR 14.88 refuelling service fee if applicable. No refund is normally due for surplus fuel. Any fuel preauthorisation must be agreed and released after settlement. Smoking is prohibited. Excessive soiling, smoke contamination or animal-related damage may lead to documented reasonable specialist-cleaning charges, not an unspecified automatic fine. Animals must be safely contained in suitable carriers, subject to lawful assistance-animal requirements. Ordinary cleaning and normal use are not treated as specialist damage.

sections.title: 14. Optional extras and safety equipment
sections.body: Subject to availability and prior confirmation: additional driver EUR 5/day; optional assistance EUR 5/day; booster EUR 5/day, maximum EUR 86.80/rental; baby/infant seat EUR 5/day, maximum EUR 86.80/rental; snow chains EUR 10/day, maximum EUR 124/rental; GPS EUR 7/day, maximum EUR 124/rental. The confirmed price remains fixed for the agreed period. All drivers must show their licences. Return equipment in its recorded condition; attributable loss or damage is charged on evidence and subject to any actual cover. Children must use restraints appropriate to their height, weight and age under current law and the manufacturer's instructions. The renter must ensure correct installation/use; this does not exclude the supplier's responsibility for defective or unsuitable equipment or its own installation/service.

sections.title: 15. Opening hours, delivery and one-way rentals
sections.body: Published normal opening hours are 08:00-21:00; confirm the issuing office's schedule and holiday arrangements. Airport, port, hotel/villa and customer delivery/collection or one-way services require an agreed location, time and final fee. Out-of-hours collection/return, when arranged: 21:01-23:59 or 06:01-07:59 EUR 25; 00:00-06:00 EUR 40. With less than 24 hours' notice the published fee is EUR 40 for an agreed out-of-hours service. These are service charges, not automatic late-return penalties; the out-of-hours waiting allowance is one hour. A charge for an unperformed service is assessed under the agreed cancellation conditions and mandatory rights.

sections.title: 16. Delays, no-show and amendments
sections.body: The normal pickup holding period is two hours after the agreed time or until closing, whichever occurs first; arranged out-of-hours waiting is one hour. Inform the office of delays; flight details assist coordination but do not replace notice. After a no-show the original vehicle is not guaranteed; any substitute and revised price require agreement. A flight diversion does not automatically transfer the booking to another location. Request pre-rental amendments in writing, normally at least 48 hours before pickup; acceptance depends on availability and written confirmation. Operational messages and written confirmations from the issuing office may document an agreed change.

sections.title: 17. Ferry permission and island travel
sections.body: Written ferry permission must specify the authorised islands/route. Published FTR charges, where agreed, are EUR 31 per direction, normally EUR 62 for a return journey, or EUR 155 for unlimited permitted ferry use during the agreed rental; ferry tickets are separate. Permission alone does not expand insurance or guarantee assistance on every island. Confirm actual ferry cover and assistance before travel. Unauthorised travel may lead to documented attributable recovery/transport charges and affect purchased cover only as permitted by the disclosed policy and law. The agreed return deadline remains in force. No automatic obligation to pay for an entire replacement vehicle arises merely from being on an island.

sections.title: 18. Keys, extensions and return time
sections.body: Notify lost, stolen or damaged keys immediately. Attributable replacement, programming and necessary recovery costs require evidence and are subject to actual cover; missing keys alone do not conclusively prove negligence or liability for every theft loss. Request an extension in writing at least 24 hours before expiry where possible. An extension is effective only after agreement of the new end date/time, total charge and mileage. A monthly extension may complete the original month rather than start a second overlapping hire. Return time is the agreed time even after delayed pickup. The normal late-return grace period is 59 minutes; after that, only the disclosed applicable daily rate and agreed extras apply, without double charging. Unauthorised retention does not create an unspecified penalty or automatic permanent blacklist.

sections.title: 19. Return location and after-hours evidence
sections.body: Return to the agreed office/carpark or another location authorised in writing. For an unauthorised return requiring collection, the published recovery/parking fee is EUR 50 plus EUR 0.56/km from the issuing station, where disclosed and reasonably applicable. Official parking fines are separate. For arranged unattended returns, record time, location, fuel, mileage and condition with photographs and use the agreed key-return procedure. Custody, risk and later damage attribution must be assessed from the agreed handover and evidence; the renter is not automatically liable for every event until the office next opens.

sections.title: 20. Cancellation, early return and non-performance
sections.body: The published booking tariff is non-refundable for customer cancellation, no-show or voluntarily unused rental days unless a more flexible written condition is agreed or mandatory rights require otherwise. This covers agreed ancillary services only to the extent lawfully payable. If AGGELOS Rentals cannot provide the agreed service and no acceptable alternative is agreed, amounts paid for the unprovided service are refunded, without excluding other mandatory rights. Refusal for a safety or documentation reason must be explained and relate to a lawful, previously disclosed requirement. There is no unrestricted company right to cancel at any time while automatically retaining all customer payments.

sections.title: 21. Fines, administration and complaints
sections.body: The renter is responsible for traffic/parking offences attributable to the rental period. Where the office actually administers a fine or violation, the published administration fee is EUR 50 per processed matter, if disclosed; it is separate from the authority's fine and must not be charged twice for the same work. Send complaints promptly, preferably within 30 days after return, to the issuing office: Piraeus piraeus@aggelosrentals.com; Antiparos/Paros aggelos@antiparosrentacar.com. A 30-day silence or later complaint does not automatically extinguish statutory claims or access to competent courts, authorities or dispute-resolution bodies.

sections.title: 22. Privacy, tracking and applicable law
sections.body: The lessor identified on the agreement is responsible for rental-related personal data. Identification, licence, contact, payment and rental/condition records are processed to perform the contract, meet legal/tax duties and, where justified, protect vehicles and establish/defend claims. Access is limited to necessary staff and service providers; relevant data may be disclosed to insurers, payment providers, professional advisers or competent authorities when lawful. Retention is limited to the applicable legal periods and necessary claim-handling purposes. Any vehicle tracking or call recording requires a specific prior notice explaining actual use, lawful basis and retention; marketing is not authorised merely by signing a rental. Applicable access, correction, erasure, restriction, portability and objection rights may be exercised through the issuing office; complaints may be made to the Hellenic Data Protection Authority (dpa.gr). Additional required privacy information, including any international transfers, must be supplied for the actual processing. Greek law applies without depriving consumers of mandatory protections or competent-jurisdiction rights. Changes apply prospectively when properly notified and agreed; no clause authorises unilateral retrospective alteration. Version AR-2026.10.29, issued 29 October 2026.
